class.name: JarBodyClouds
class.brief_description: Volumetric clouds above the body's sea level.
class.description: A layer of clouds between [member altitude] and [member altitude] + [member thickness] meters above sea level (a spherical shell, or a slab on a flat body). Where clouds are comes from the planet's weather map, made in C++ at startup (a cube map, about half a second, no baking; [member seed]): climate zones with noisy borders (storm clusters along the equator, mostly clear subtropics with fields of trade cumulus and cellular low cloud, cyclones with spiral arms and fronts drawn out east to west in the storm belts, stratus over the poles), how high the tops reach and how sheet-like they are. It drifts slowly around the planet. Near the camera (up to the material's [code]volume_distance[/code]) the clouds are ray marched through tileable 3D Perlin-Worley noise: rounded bases, domed tops, eroded edges, lit through the cloud towards the sun with silver linings, approximate multiple scattering, sky light, the planet's shadow and moonlight. Beyond that, and always from orbit, they are drawn as one look-up where the view crosses the layer (the covered part of the pixel, lit with the relief of the map's tops): the same weather, at a fraction of the cost. The two dissolve into each other. Beyond the far plane they are drawn in scaled space with the rest of the body. Coverage, sizes, density, wind, colors and quality are set on [member material].

method.name: get_weather
method.description: The weather map in use (a [Cubemap]: r coverage, g how high the tops reach, b how sheet-like), made at the layer's first update; null on flat bodies.

method.name: get_active_material
method.description: The material in use: [member material] or the default.

members.member: Height of the bottom of the cloud layer above sea level, in meters.
Which weather: the weather map is made from it (cyclones, cloud fields).
Height of the layer from its bottom to its top, in meters.
The clouds' look. Empty: the default [code]clouds.gdshader[/code].
